claims.source: USPTO application data for 14/807943 (product PTGRXML, data.uspto.gov), retrieved from the file wrapper 28 August 2026
claims.text: The prosecution was short and uncontested. One non-final rejection was written on 12 June 2018 and mailed 20 June 2018; an applicant-initiated telephonic interview followed on 10 July 2018; the applicant responded on 19 July 2018; and the Notice of Allowability was signed on 13 September 2018. There was no final rejection, no affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.132, no Notice of Appeal and no appeal brief.

claims.source: USPTO file wrapper, application 14/807,943, Notice of Allowability (PTOL-37) signed 13 September 2018 (Paper No. 20180913) and Notice of Allowance and Fee(s) Due (PTOL-85) mailed 10 October 2018, examiner Thomas M. Dougherty; transcribed at research/patents/wrapper/pax182-notice-of-allowability-2018-09-13.txt
claims.text: The reason given for allowance is novelty over the prior art and nothing else: 'The following is an examiner's statement of reasons for allowance: the prior art fails to show a high energy electromagnetic field generator, comprising: a shell, the shell having embedded polycrystalline ferroelectric ceramic material, the material being polarized such that the ceramic material exhibits strong Piezoelectric Effect properties thus inducing high frequency vibrations'. Claims 1-12 were allowed. The only change made was an examiner's amendment deleting one line of claim 11 'to correct a typographical error'.

connections.label: Salvatore Cezar Pais
connections.note: Application 14/807943, assigned to the Secretary of the Navy.

desc: The earliest of the five filings and the foundation of the set, since every later device depends on generating and manipulating high-energy electromagnetic fields. Application 14/807943, filed 24 July 2015, granted 20 November 2018, assigned to the Secretary of the Navy. The abstract describes a generator comprising a shell, an electrostatic generator, a power plant and a thermoelectric generator. Its file wrapper was obtained and read on 28 August 2026 and it is the control case for the craft application. One non-final rejection, one telephone interview, one response, and allowance on the ground that the prior art did not show the device. Enablement was never raised. A different examiner in a different art unit handled it, and it too has now lapsed for non-payment of the first maintenance fee.

timeline.label: The only rejection the electromagnetic field generator ever drew
timeline.text: USPTO mailed the single non-final rejection in application 14/807943. A telephone interview followed on 10 July and the applicant responded on 19 July. Enablement was never raised in this case.

timeline.label: Electromagnetic field generator allowed on prior art, not on enablement
timeline.text: The Notice of Allowability for application 14/807943 allowed claims 1-12 because 'the prior art fails to show' the claimed generator. The craft application, which incorporates this generator by reference, was under appeal at that moment for being impossible.

timeline.label: US 10,135,366 expires for non-payment of maintenance fees
timeline.text: The first of the two granted Pais patents lapsed for non-payment of the first maintenance fee, five weeks before the inertial mass reduction patent did the same. USPTO had mailed a maintenance fee reminder on 11 July 2022.
